title: POC scoping: cost modeling & unit economics with Atlas Cloud
summary: High-level POC scoping focused on cost modeling for a 6-week pilot. Discussed success criteria (latency < 200ms p50, throughput 100 qps, end-to-end cost targets), workload sizing, benchmark plan, batching/caching knobs, and a proposed timeline and deliverables. Action items: share benchmark harness, pricing spreadsheet, and security pack; schedule infra access and initial run next week.
topics: Per-token cost estimates and batching/caching options
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're at, uh, 16:00 PT, I'll kick off. Quick intros?
[00:10] Laura Kim: Hi, Laura Kim, CTO at Atlas Cloud.
[00:15] Miguel Santos: Miguel, platform eng, I manage infra and cost models.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Priya, ML engineer, working on our recommender and support use-cases.
[00:22] Samir Patel: Great, Jia, do you want to intro?
[00:25] Jia Chen: Sure, Jia Chen, Solutions Eng at Redwood, focus on perf and private deployments.
[00:30] Samir Patel: Cool. The purpose today is to scope a POC around cost modeling — figure out the unit economics, get some benchmark runs, and define success criteria. We have about 45 minutes.
[00:40] Laura Kim: Sounds good. We're mainly evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private — we care a lot about predictable cost and data residency. We have a, uh, budget we want to hit for the pilot.
[00:52] Miguel Santos: To be concrete, for the first POC we plan to run two workloads: a support chat assistant (interactive, lots of short sessions) and a nightly batch rerank for recommendations (longer context, higher token counts).
[01:05] Priya Rao: For the chat, typical turn length is 20-40 tokens and we target ~1200 sessions per minute during peak. For rerank, about 2k tokens per request but only ~30 requests/min.
[01:18] Jia Chen: Great — that split is useful. For cost modeling we usually estimate per-input token + output token unit economics, then apply batching and KV/prefix caching for the rerank. Also consider latency SLOs — can you share target latency?
[01:28] Laura Kim: Our SLA goal is p50 < 200ms and p95 < 450ms for chat. For rerank latency can be higher — p95 under 2s is acceptable.
[01:40] Samir Patel: Okay, success criteria then: 1) latency targets, 2) match/beat baseline accuracy on our eval set, 3) total cost <= $X/month for pilot — Laura, you said a pilot budget, what's that number?
[01:52] Laura Kim: We're aiming at roughly $15k for a 6-week pilot, not including any one-time setup fees. That's a hard constraint.
[02:01] Miguel Santos: Important: we need encryption with KMS + audit logs. Also we plan to test both hosted and private (VPC) modes if possible, but we need to see cost delta.
[02:14] Jia Chen: Noted. We'll share SOC2/ISO docs and the security pack — link in the follow-up. For the costing, quick back-of-envelope: for chat small-turn workload, if you use a 70B-class open model quantized on GPUs, our per-token inference cost ballpark is $0.0003 to $0.0006 per token depending on batching and caching. If you use a smaller 13B model it falls to ~ $0.00008-$0.00018. That's raw compute — networking, storage and overhead add on.
[02:44] Priya Rao: That delta is big. How deterministic are those numbers? We care about predictability.
[02:50] Jia Chen: They're estimates from our benchmark atlas; variance depends on sequence length distribution and batching. For interactive chat, batching is limited so you see higher per-token. For rerank you can batch larger. Caching the prefix (embeddings or KV cache) for repeated contexts can slash cost by up to 40% for you'd see a lot of identical prompts.
[03:06] Samir Patel: One nuance — model family choice matters for latency/cost/quality tradeoff. We should plan two tracks: model A (13B) cheaper, likely meets latency; model B (70B) for accuracy testing. We'll run the benchmark harness on both.
[03:21] Laura Kim: Timeline? We want results before our budget review in 6 weeks.
[03:26] Samir Patel: Proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) — access & dataset ingest; week 1 — baseline runs and small-scale perf tests; week 2-3 — full benchmark and tuning (batching, kernel configs); week 4 — accuracy evaluation and cost extrapolation; week 5 — final report and decision. That's a 6-week loop including buffer.
[03:42] Miguel Santos: For infra access, we'll need a limited VPC peering or temporary keys for hosted tests. Security team will want an architecture diagram.
[03:50] Jia Chen: We'll provide a template for the architecture diagram and a minimal-privilege role for the benchmark runner.
[03:55] Priya Rao: On benchmarks: what's your harness look like? We need reproducible numbers to plug into our cost model.
[04:02] Jia Chen: Our harness simulates traffic profiles, measures per-token latency, throughput, GPU utilization, memory, and token-level costs. We run warm and cold sequence tests, and we can simulate different batching windows (10ms, 25ms, 50ms). We also capture token generation distribution and KV cache hit rates.
[04:18] Samir Patel: We'll ask you to run three scenarios: interactive (low-batch), batch-rerank (high-seq, high-batch), and mixed. For each we'll produce per-token cost, tokens/sec, and recommended batching/caching knobs.
[04:30] Laura Kim: How do you convert those per-token numbers into monthly cost? We need a spreadsheet showing expected monthly QPS and cost.
[04:36] Jia Chen: We'll provide a pricing spreadsheet: inputs are QPS, avg input/output tokens, cache hit rate, batching window and model selection. The sheet will output compute cost, expected infra (dedicated GPU hours if you choose reserved), and total monthly. We'll also show sensitivity analysis — e.g., if QPS doubles.
[04:52] Miguel Santos: On reserved capacity — if we do dedicated, how do you size the pool? We want to avoid overcommit.
[04:58] Jia Chen: We recommend sizing to 95th percentile throughput with a burst buffer. We'll show two sizing options: conservative (headroom for spikes) and tight (cost optimized). Dedicated pricing has commit discounts — we'll model both.
[05:10] Priya Rao: Any gotchas around batching latency tradeoff? For chat we can't add large batching windows.
[05:15] Jia Chen: Right — interactive SLOs limit batch windows. For p50 <200ms you'd typically keep batching at 10-25ms depending on traffic; this gives modest batching gains. For the rerank, you can use 50-200ms buffers and much higher batch sizes. Also prefix caching helps for repeated histories.
[05:30] Samir Patel: Let's talk numbers for Atlas' stated load. Priya said 1200 sessions/min at peak with 1.5 turns per session avg => that's 1800 turns/min, roughly 30 req/sec. With 30 req/sec and 30 tokens output avg, that's 900 tokens/sec. If per-token is $0.0002 that's $0.18/sec or about $13k/month, ignoring some overhead — hmm that starts to approach your pilot budget.
[06:02] Miguel Santos: Good calc. For rerank, 30 req/min at 2000 tokens ~ 60k tokens/min ~ 1k tokens/sec similar order. So combined costs matter.
[06:12] Jia Chen: Exactly; combined these could be in the $20k/mo ballpark at certain model choices. But with batching and caching, we can potentially cut 25-40% for rerank and 10-20% for chat, depending on cache hit.
[06:26] Laura Kim: So practically, how do we ensure we don't blow the $15k pilot?
[06:30] Samir Patel: Options: 1) use smaller model (13B) for chat, reserve 70B for rerank or eval; 2) aggressive caching for repetitive prompts; 3) limit pilot query volume or schedule runs off-peak; 4) use dedicated reserved capacity with commit discount if you expect steady load. We'll model these in the spreadsheet.
[06:50] Priya Rao: About accuracy: our baseline F1 is 0.74 on the support intents. We need to be within 2 points of that.
[06:57] Jia Chen: We'll include baseline replication as part of the POC. For accuracy regressions we flag and can roll back to a different model variant.
[07:05] Miguel Santos: Security: SSO/SAML and KMS — we need SAML, KMS, and audit logging, plus data residency in us-east-1. Can Redwood support that in hosted?
[07:16] Jia Chen: Hosted supports SAML and KMS integration; for strict data residency and air-gapped needs we'd recommend Private (VPC) deployment. We'll detail options and incremental costs.
[07:28] Samir Patel: Ok. Let's commit to concrete next steps. Jia, you'll run an initial baseline this week with small sample from Atlas?
[07:35] Jia Chen: Yes, if you can share a small sanitized sample dataset and an auth handle, we can run baseline within 3 business days.
[07:42] Laura Kim: We can share a 5k example convo set and a sample rerank dataset. We'll sanitize PII.
[07:48] Samir Patel: Great. We'll also send the pricing spreadsheet, benchmark harness link, and security pack.
[07:55] Priya Rao: For the harness, can we run it on our infra if we do private?
[07:59] Jia Chen: Yes, the harness can be run by your team with our scripts; we can provide a dockerized runner and a runbook.
[08:06] Miguel Santos: About logging — we need token-level cost breakdowns per route. Is that available?
[08:11] Jia Chen: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token cost and latency, and we can export traces for the POC.
[08:17] Samir Patel: Any competitor mentions? Laura?
[08:20] Laura Kim: We're also evaluating Anthropic and AWS offerings, mainly to compare total cost and compliance.
[08:26] Jia Chen: Noted. We'll prepare a comparative note but we won't replicate their numbers exactly.
[08:31] Samir Patel: Let's wrap with explicit next steps and owners.
[08:35] Laura Kim: Sounds good.
[08:36] Samir Patel: Okay: 1) Atlas to send sample datasets and SSO requirements (owner: Laura) 2) Redwood to send pricing spreadsheet and security pack (owner: Samir) 3) Redwood to run baseline harness on small sample (owner: Jia) 4) Schedule infra access meeting for next Tue (owner: Samir/Miguel).
[08:55] Priya Rao: We should capture an action item to define the eval set and success metrics — I'll own that.
[09:02] Miguel Santos: Also I'll confirm access method (VPC peering vs token).
[09:06] Samir Patel: Great. We'll aim to have the baseline report and cost extrapolation by end of next week. Thanks everyone.
[09:14] Laura Kim: Thanks all.
[09:16] (meeting ends)

Redwood to send pricing spreadsheet, benchmark harness link, and security pack (owner: Samir)
Jia to run baseline harness on small sample and share results within 3 business days (owner: Jia)
